title: On-call shift notes and SLO review — Sept 02 2026
content:
TL;DR:
- Overnight (2026-09-01 23:40–00:20 UTC) we saw a spike in 95th latency and a small increase in 5xx rate for the embeddings service (embedder-v2). Root cause appears to be a bad quantized kernel landing in the serving-runtime image used by the dedicated embedder pool.

Shift summary (09/02 oncall: Aisha -> Connor handoff):
- 23:33 UTC: first signs of queue growth on embedder pool E2; alerts fired (latency_p95 > 400ms, request_queue_depth > 50).
- 23:40 UTC: traffic routing switched to fallback model variant (embedder-v1-quant-stable) by automatic fallback policy; error rate briefly increased as some clients retried.
- 23:55 UTC: rollback of serving-runtime image (tag: 2026-09-01-optimized) on dedicated pool to previous stable (2026-08-24-stable).
- 00:05 UTC: quick verification load: p95 returned to baseline; error rate dropped below SLO threshold.
- 00:20 UTC: incident declared resolved; oncall postmortem ticket created (INFRA-4392).

Incident details (short):
- Impact: 6% of embedder requests experienced p95 latency > 400ms for ~45 minutes; 5xx spiked to 0.9% (SLO = 0.5%). No customer data leak, no retries lost.
- Root cause hypothesis: new quantized attention kernel introduced a pathological code path when sequence length > 2048 and batch mixing occurred; triggered on a small fraction of production traffic patterns.
- Contributing factors: automatic image rollout to a subset of dedicated nodes (canary pool size set to 10% but some nodes incorrectly labeled as canary), limited pre-deploy perf smoke for long-seq mixes.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Auto-fallback triggered (config: route to embedder-v1-quant-stable) — prevented wider impact.
- Manual rollback of serving-runtime image on affected dedicated pool.
- Expanded Canary label scan to detect mis-labeled nodes (see action items).

SLO snapshot (24h window ending 2026-09-02 06:00 UTC):
- embeddings.latency.p95: baseline 210ms -> incident peak 480ms (returned to 220ms after rollback).
- embeddings.error_rate.5xx: baseline 0.14% -> peak 0.92% (SLO threshold 0.5%).
- availability (successful token responses): stayed above 99.85% overall.

Post-incident action items (owners):
- INFRA-4392 (postmortem ticket) -> write full timeline + attach heap/profile dumps (owner: Marcus Chen, due: 2026-09-06).
- Fix canary labeling script to ensure node metadata accuracy (owner: Leah Wong, PR: serving-runtime#3210, due: 2026-09-04).
- Add long-sequence mixed-batch smoke test to CI for quantized kernels (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-09-10).
- Add alert suppression window for controlled rollouts to avoid transient cascading alerts (owner: Connor Reed, due: 2026-09-07).

Operational notes / playbook updates (quick wins):
- Playbook: `embedder-high-latency` updated with explicit rollback steps and who to page for image rollbacks.
- Observability: added a short-lived metric `embedder.canary_mismatch_count` (counts nodes reporting mismatched image tags vs canary label).
- Console: annotated model-catalog entry for embedder-v2 recommending staged rollout flags.

On-call handoff checklist (what I told Connor during H2):
- Watch `embedder.canary_mismatch_count` and `embedder.request_queue_depth`. If mismatch_count > 0, pause rollouts immediately.
- If p95 > 350ms for > 10 minutes AND queue_depth increasing, run fallback: `/infra/route/fallback embedder embedder-v1-quant-stable`.
- For rollbacks, use the deploy dashboard rollback action (do NOT manually SSH nodes unless SRE lead directs).
- Post-incident: attach the dump at INFRA-4392 and ping #sre-oncall for review.

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts:
- We should evaluate isolating long-seq traffic onto separate pools (traffic classifier) so quant kernel regressions don't impact short-seq paths.
- Consider adding a small synthetic traffic generator that can probe rare code-paths (seq>2048 with batch-mix) once per deploy. Cheap and would have caught this.
- The automatic fallback mechanism worked well; need to cover the labeling edge-case in the runbook.

Follow-ups for next week (prioritized):
1) Canary label fix (blocks safe rollouts) — high priority.
2) Long-seq smoke test in CI — medium priority.
3) Add a brief runbook QA step before controlled rollouts (owner: release-engineering).
4) Evaluate SLA credit exposure and customer comms with CS for any accounts that may have hit degraded performance (owner: Leah Wong + CS).

Attachments / links (internal):
- INFRA-4392 (atlassian): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4392
- Postmortem draft (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/Embedder+Regressions+Postmortem
- Runtime PR with canary-label fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3210
- Slack thread: #sre-ops, thread-8b2f5 (has debug logs + flamegraphs)

Misc meeting notes (today's sync with release + runtime teams, 09/02 09:30 UTC):
- Release: agreed to pause further embedder-v2 rollouts until long-seq test is in place.
- Runtime: will instrument kernel to log offending sequence lengths when a fallback branch is taken — helpful for root cause.
- CS: asked SRE to surface any customers who saw degraded tokens beyond baseline; Leah to coordinate.

Open questions / risks:
- Could other quant kernels share the same failure mode? Need a small audit of recent kernel changes.
- How to avoid noisy alerts during controlled rollouts without blinding on-call? (proposal: add rollout label and tie alert suppression to rollout=active).

Quick retrospective comment: fallback + rollback was fast and prevented a larger outage. Pain points were rollout labeling and lack of specific smoke tests. If we address those two, the risk profile of kernel-level perf regressions drops substantially.

Handoff signature:
- Aisha P. (oncall -> Connor R.) 2026-09-02 08:15 UTC
- Connor acknowledged and took responsibility for 2026-09-02 08:20 UTC.

END OF NOTE

(Informal scratch area below — keep for context; delete before finalizing postmortem)
- temp commands used: `kubectl -n serving rollout undo deployment/embedder-dedicated --to-revision=2026-08-24-stable` (used via deploy dashboard).
- grep of logs for offending seq lengths: `jq '.request.seq_len' embedder-logs | sort | uniq -c | tail -n 20` -> handful of seqs > 2048 clustered to one client pool.
- next week: pair with runtime folks on kernel instrumentation (timeboxed 2h).
